strategies.name: Naive 8-stage serial all-reduce
strategies.desc: Directly transcribes the reference: 8 sequential all_reduce calls with intermediate bidiagonal coupling/decoupling loops. Total 8 all_reduce dispatches on full W*S tensor. Maximizes readability but no optimization; represents the baseline latency-bound approach where each stage waits for the previous collective to complete.

strategies.name: Fused bidiagonal transform per stage
strategies.desc: Merge the forward bidiagonal coupling, all_reduce, and backward decoupling into minimal buffer writes per stage. Still 8 all_reduce dispatches but eliminates redundant /W divisions and reduces local compute overhead by fusing the coupling logic into single-pass loops. Trades code clarity for reduced memory bandwidth on local operations.

strategies.name: Reduce-scatter + all-gather decomposition
strategies.desc: Replace each full all_reduce with reduce_scatter (producing local shard) followed by all_gather to reconstruct the global view. Each stage becomes 2 collectives (16 total dispatches) but each operates on W*S/W = S-sized payloads for reduce_scatter, potentially leveraging better network topology utilization. Trades dispatch count for smaller per-dispatch message size.

strategies.name: Pipelined overlapping with async launch
strategies.desc: Attempt to overlap computation and communication by splitting the W*S tensor into chunks and issuing non-blocking collectives where supported. Launch next stage's bidiagonal transform on already-available data while current all_reduce completes on remaining chunks. Expected 8+ dispatches with potential latency hiding, trading synchronization complexity for throughput.

strategies.name: Hierarchical two-level reduction within nodes
strategies.desc:
Exploit the multi-node topology (assuming nodes contain multiple ranks): perform intra-node local reductions first (e.g., shared memory or node-local all_reduce), then inter-node all_reduce, then broadcast within node. For 8 stages this becomes 8 * (intra-reduce + inter-reduce + intra-broadcast) ≈ 24 dispatches on smaller cross-node payloads. Optimizes for inter-node bandwidth bottleneck at cost of higher dispatch overhead.
